title: Association Between Aging and Specific Physiological Measurements
archive_status: Data preservation is complete. All datasets are publicly available.
notes: Downloaded: tabular files (xls/xlsx/csv/txt) and PDF reports up to 50 MB. Every Excel sheet is also saved as '<file>__<sheet>.csv' (raw cell grid, no header detection).
Not downloaded: figure images (tif/jpg) - they are rendered graphs; their URLs are listed under skipped_files.
Downloaded files are untrusted data: parse only, never open macros / execute.

LSAH newsletter (Oct 1998, vol 7(2)) tables: mean values by 5-year age band for female/male astronauts vs female/male comparison group. No per-person data, no flight-relative time points. Not importable to observation; usable as population reference curves.

files.dataset_name: Blood Pressure-Mean Values by Age in the Longitudinal Study for Astronaut Health (LSAH)  Population
files.dataset_description:
The graph shows mean values by age for sitting diastolic and systolic blood pressure in the Longitudinal Study of Astronaut Health (LSAH) population: female and male astronauts, and female and male comparison subjects.

Source: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Association between aging and specific physiological measurements. In: Longitudinal Study of Astronaut Health Newsletter. October 1998;7(2).

files.dataset_name: Hearing-Mean Values by Age in the Longitudinal Study for Astronaut Health (LSAH)  Population
files.dataset_description:
The graph shows mean values by age for hearing in the Longitudinal Study of Astronaut Health (LSAH) population: female and male astronauts, and female and male comparison subjects. Hearing was measured in the right ear at 6000 Hz.

Source: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Association between aging and specific physiological measurements. In: Longitudinal Study of Astronaut Health Newsletter. October 1998;7(2).

files.dataset_name: LDL Cholesterol-Mean Values by Age in the Longitudinal Study for Astronaut Health (LSAH)  Population

Source: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Association between aging and specific physiological measurements. In: Longitudinal Study of Astronaut Health Newsletter. October 1998;7(2).
